captions.source: The hook: the warning box on the label is empty. Roundup's US label carries no cancer warning; after Monsanto v. Durnell (25 Jun 2026) a state-law claim cannot require one, and the label is set under federal law (EPA). The jug on screen is generic (WEEDKILLER · GLYPHOSATE HERBICIDE); Roundup is named in the caption and the tag only.

About 65,000 Roundup claims (Reuters via Insurance Journal, 3 Nov 2026; Bayer, Mar 2026): plaintiffs allege glyphosate caused their non-Hodgkin lymphoma. 'Say' is the caption's verb for the allegation; the tag says PLAINTIFFS ALLEGE. Bayer says Roundup is safe; the EPA (and EFSA) did not find glyphosate likely carcinogenic; IARC classified it 'probably carcinogenic to humans' in 2015. Search summaries only.

Monsanto Co. v. Durnell, No. 24-1068, decided 25 Jun 2026, 7–2 (Kavanaugh; Jackson and Gorsuch dissenting): FIFRA preempts a Missouri failure-to-warn claim that would have required a cancer warning on Roundup's label; a jury award of about $1.25M was reversed (Mayer Brown, Faegre Drinker, National Ag Law Center summaries). 'A state warning? No' = a state-law claim cannot require one. Search summaries only.

Calley Means, former White House adviser (left 22 Oct 2026), on The Joe Rogan Experience #2578 (reported 6 Nov 2026: Axios, STAT, The Hill, Yahoo News): he alleges Kennedy was not consulted when the White House backed the glyphosate makers at the Supreme Court or on the executive order, and that Wiles's deputies pushed the order as 'nonnegotiable'. Attributed allegation. Beside it, on tags: Kennedy's own account (E&E News, 5 Mar 2026: 'I did know about the executive order, and I made my opinions about it clear to the administration'); the White House's reply citing 'extensive victories for the MAHA agenda' and aide James Blair's 'no idea what Calley Means is talking about' (STAT, The Hill, Axios, 6 Nov 2026). 'Told RFK Jr. not to call the president' appears only in an advocacy group's clip (MAHA Action on X), so it is not used. Not used: Stephen Miller replacing Susie Wiles (6 Nov); no link is claimed or shown. Search summaries only.

The station's line, in the deadpan of a legal document ('this page intentionally left blank'); true as a description: Roundup's US label carries no cancer warning, and after Durnell a state claim cannot require one. The EPA's position is that glyphosate is not likely carcinogenic. Bayer's $7.25B class settlement for current and future claims awaits final approval in St. Louis; Bayer's CEO said on 3 Nov he expects it before Christmas (Reuters via Insurance Journal); no ruling as of 7 Nov (search summaries: Claims Journal, Global Agriculture, Settlement Insight).

post.en: Roundup's label has no cancer warning: the Supreme Court says states can't require one (7–2). A February order made glyphosate a defense priority. An ex-adviser alleges RFK Jr. wasn't consulted; Kennedy says he knew; the White House disputes it. Bayer: safe. Who writes the label?

stamp.en: NATIONAL DEFENSE PRIORITY · EXECUTIVE ORDER · 18 FEB 2026, a red rubber stamp on the label
stamp.why: Executive order of 18 Feb 2026, 'Promoting the National Defense by Ensuring an Adequate Supply of Elemental Phosphorus and Glyphosate-Based Herbicides', invoking the Defense Production Act (Washington Times, Fresh Fruit Portal, ADN, Feb 2026). The stamp on screen reads NATIONAL DEFENSE PRIORITY, a paraphrase; the tag gives the order's date and the act. MAHA activists objected; Kennedy backed it publicly and later told Rogan he was not 'particularly happy' with it. Search summaries only.
